news.title: vLLM v0.33.0rc3 expands model serving and changes CUDA packaging
news.summary: The v0.33.0rc3 release candidate adds model and speculative-decoding support, moves to PyTorch 2.14, and publishes CUDA 13 rather than CUDA 12.9 artifacts, alongside AMD ROCm updates.
news.why_it_matters: Inference engineers need to validate model support, compatibility and deployment images before upgrading serving fleets.
news.caveat: This specific URL is tagged rc3 (release candidate), even though its GitHub heading says v0.33.0; performance claims are release-note benchmarks on specified hardware.

news.title: InvokeAI 6.14.3 adds editable vector layers for image workflows
news.summary: InvokeAI's 6.14.3 patch adds editable vector shapes and splines to its Canvas, which artists can rasterize for image-to-image workflows, and fixes resumed model downloads.
news.why_it_matters: This bridges precise vector composition and local generative image editing without forcing every shape to be raster-first.
news.caveat: This is a product-specific patch, not evidence that image-generation quality or speed improved across models; GitHub displays release time without an explicit timezone.

news.title: Windmill 1.856.0 adds external OIDC token support for MCP access
news.summary: Windmill's 1.856.0 release adds support for MCP access tokens from external OIDC issuers, HashiCorp Vault references, workspace-role sync through the CLI, and working folders/instructions for AI sessions.
news.why_it_matters: It gives teams more options for authenticated and governed automation workflows that expose tools to agents.
news.caveat: The announcement is a release-note claim, not an independent security audit; organizational authentication still requires appropriate configuration.

news.title: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx benchmark for tool-using agents
news.summary: SemiAnalysis published GDPx, a tool-using agent benchmark spanning 11 specialized domains, including chip design, cybersecurity, biology and alignment. The authors report a 12% top score on their own aggregate evaluation.
news.why_it_matters: Environment-based tasks and explicit grading constraints offer ways to evaluate agent capability and boundary-following beyond static question-answer tests.
news.caveat: The 12% figure and comparisons are publisher-run, not independently replicated. Domain weighting, model harnesses, safety refusals and grading design affect results; alignment and cyber exercises are controlled evaluations, not real deployment incidents.

news.title: WIRED investigates disguised apps linked to abusive deepfake services
news.summary: WIRED reports that researchers linked more than 400 app and web-domain properties to services presenting ordinary AI tools while conditionally exposing nonconsensual explicit deepfake functions. The investigation describes app-store and advertising distribution.
news.why_it_matters: The reported pattern raises difficult questions about app review, server-switched features, consent safeguards and enforcement across advertising platforms.
news.caveat: These are findings attributed to WIRED and its interviewed researchers, not a fresh independent Atlas audit. The 400-plus figure covers linked domains and apps, not 400 individually verified malicious applications; the reporting does not identify a particular underlying model.

news.title: South Korea proposes larger 2027 AI investment in record budget
news.summary: Reuters reports President Lee Jae Myung urged lawmakers to approve a proposed 2027 budget including 21.3 trillion won for AI and major projects in semiconductors, physical AI and data centres—nearly twice this year's comparable investment.
news.why_it_matters: The proposed allocation signals a national policy priority for AI infrastructure and hardware, but it still depends on the budget process.
news.caveat: This is a proposed budget and presidential statement reported by Reuters, not enacted spending or proof the projects will be completed. Atlas has not independently checked the underlying budget documents.

news.title: ADNOC and G42 announce an enterprise AI agreement with OpenAI
news.summary: Reuters reports Abu Dhabi's energy company ADNOC and AI company G42 signed an agreement with OpenAI at the ADIPEC conference to use frontier AI in ADNOC operations.
news.why_it_matters: The announced agreement illustrates growing enterprise interest in deploying advanced AI models in energy-sector workflows.
news.caveat: Reuters reports an agreement and company statements, not independently demonstrated performance, deployment success or realized productivity gains. Specific systems and safeguards have not been audited by Atlas.

news.title: ECB vice-president warns of high AI equity valuations among stability risks
news.summary: Reuters quotes ECB Vice-President Boris Vujcic describing elevated AI-stock valuations, bond-market stress and potential losses at nonbank lenders and funds as present financial-stability concerns.
news.why_it_matters: AI spending and expected returns increasingly matter beyond model developers, including investors, infrastructure financing and financial oversight.
news.caveat: This is a reported risk assessment, not proof of an AI-stock bubble or a prediction of an imminent crash. The ECB's full Financial Stability Review was scheduled for November 18.

news.title: Oracle outlines a $20 billion debt-and-equity financing plan
news.summary: Reuters reports Oracle plans to seek approximately $20 billion in debt and equity financing, potentially supporting its AI and cloud infrastructure expansion as well as other corporate uses.
news.why_it_matters: The plan shows the scale and financing pressure of major AI infrastructure buildouts.
news.caveat: The $20 billion is a reported financing plan, not completed proceeds or a dedicated $20 billion AI-only budget. Final offering terms and uses were not established at publication; Atlas has not independently reviewed all cited filings.
